clauses.clause: Preamble: designates John D. Biggers Administrator of the census under the act of Aug. 30, 1937
Para. 1: Administrator authorized and directed to conduct the census and, on completion, issue a report of findings
Para. 2: Administrator may appoint temporary employees, fix pay without regard to the Classification Act, and make necessary expenditures
Final para.: allocations up to $5,000,000 from the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1937 will be made for census expenses

conclusion.basis_rule: open: rule (e) performance not proved by an accepted source

data_errors: Evidence slice (finding aid later-events, from OFR notes) records EO 7999 as an 'amendment' of EO 7711. The EO 7999 text contains no textual amendment of EO 7711; it transfers the office's records and property and grants a conditional civil-service exception. Whether the classification is right in a broader sense is not settled; rule (d) is not relied on.
APP transcription of EO 7711 misspells the name as 'John D. Biggets'; the Federal Register printing reads 'Biggers'.
jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_7711.txt runs on into the neighbouring Civil Air Regulations document on the same page (expected, noted in the file header); order number OCR reads '[No. 77111'.
EO 7999's footnote citing EO 7711 reads '12 F. R. 1891 (2221 D I)' in OCR, i.e. footnote 1, 2 F.R. 1891 (2221 DI).

The catalogue record (mocat.library.unt.edu/catalog/523-ch298) again returned HTTP 403; the 13 May 1938 press conference transcription says the printed report was still to come.

gaps.what: No express named revocation or supersession of EO 7711 found in the instruments inspected (EO 7711, EO 7999, the act of Aug. 30, 1937). The formal status is a bounded search finding only.

moves.note: Rule (e) needs a source for performance. The held EO 7999 proves only that the office's records and property went to Commerce effective 1938-11-01 and that four named employees may be appointed to the classified service; it does not say the census and report duties were completed. The statutory deadline of 1938-04-01 does not prove completion. The only performance evidence found is a transcription lead (FDR press conference, 13 May 1938), which says the census was taken and the printed report was still to be submitted. The catalogue record for the final report could not be opened (HTTP 403). Status is therefore OPEN, not NO.
Not reached. Para. 1, para. 2 and the funding paragraph all lack a quoted ending source.

propositions.claim: EO 7711 is printed in the Federal Register of Friday, 24 Sept. 1937 (vol. 2, no. 185) at page 2221, dated at the White House 22 Sept. 1937 and filed 23 Sept. 1937.
propositions.quote: [F. R. Doc. 37-2823; Filed, September 23,1937; 12:30 p. m.]

propositions.claim: The order designates a named person, John D. Biggers, as Administrator of the census.
propositions.quote: I hereby designate as Administrator thereof John D. Biggers and delegate to him the following functions and duties

propositions.claim: Para. 1 directs the census and a report on its completion. It does not itself show performance.
propositions.quote: is authorized and directed to conduct the said census and upon completion thereof to issue a report of findings

propositions.claim: Para. 2 authorizes temporary staff and expenditures as necessary to carry out the 1937 act.
propositions.quote: authorized to appoint, as temporary employees, and fix the compensation, without regard to the Classification Act of 1923

propositions.claim: The final paragraph provides funding of up to $5,000,000 from the 1937 relief appropriation.
propositions.quote: in a total amount not exceeding $5,000,000 from the appropriation contained in the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1937

propositions.claim: EO 7999 (31 Oct. 1938, 3 FR 2603) transferred all records and property of the Administrator's office to the Secretary of Commerce effective 1 Nov. 1938, naming EO 7711. It does not terminate the authorities in EO 7711.
propositions.quote: established by Executive Order No. 7711, of September 22, 1937,1 pursuant to the act approved August 30, 1937 (50 Stat. 883), shall be transferred effective as of November 1, 1938

propositions.claim: EO 7999 permits four named employees who served under the Administrator to be appointed to classified civil-service positions without competitive examination, subject to their establishing qualifications. This is a conditional permission; it does not show that their service or the Administrator's duties had ended.
propositions.quote: who have served with merit under the said Administrator, may be appointed to appropriate positions in the classified civil service without compliance with the competitive requirements of the Civil Service Rules, subject to their establishing requisite qualifications

propositions.claim: The authorizing act required the census to be taken on or before 1 April 1938 (50 Stat. 883). This is a deadline; it proves neither completion nor expiry.
propositions.quote: the President shall cause to be taken on or before April 1, 1938, a census of partial and total unemployment, and occupations

propositions.claim: EO 7999 contains no words expressly revoking, superseding or textually amending EO 7711; its operative provisions are a transfer of records and property and a conditional civil-service appointment permission. This does not settle whether the finding aid's 'amendment' classification is right in a broader sense.
propositions.quote: shall be transferred effective as of November 1, 1938, to the custody and control of the Secretary of Commerce

propositions.claim: The act sets no express termination date for the administering agency; it provides for temporary personnel.
propositions.quote: temporary personnel required to carry out the purposes of this Act shall be appointed without regard to the Classification Act of 1923

propositions.claim: LEAD ONLY (American Presidency Project transcription, read through the fetch tool's summarizer, so wording needs checking against the page): at his press conference of 13 May 1938 the President described a letter from Biggers as a semi-final report, said the census had been taken in the first week of December, that the staff was substantially disbanded, that unspent money would return to the Treasury, and that the printed report was still to be submitted. This suggests the census was conducted but shows the final report had not yet been issued on that date; it is not an accepted original and does not prove performance.
propositions.quote: The printed report will be submitted shortly and made public.

review.conclusion_reason: NO under performance requires evidence of completed performance. Neither the census deadline nor transfer of records/property proves that the census and report duties ended by November 1, 1938. The result itself leaves hiring/expenditure and funding authorities open. The supported disposition is OPEN, pending evidence of report issuance and disposition of remaining authorities. No express ending was found in the inspected instruments, supporting formal status only as that bounded search finding. T2 is supported; the submitted NO assessment fails T3.
review.stop_code_verdict: confirmed: WEB fits the first gap. The evidence slice supplies no final report or proof of issuance; the held transfer order does not resolve that fact, and the cited external catalogue remains inaccessible.
review.suspected_defect: The categorical NO and asserted latest ending date contradict the result's explicit unresolved performance and authority gaps. It also converts conditional appointment permission in EO 7999 into actual staff movement.

verdicts.reason: Held Federal Register OCR confirms publication date, page 2221, and signature date; the filing quotation alone does not establish all three.
Held original expressly designates John D. Biggers Administrator.
Paragraph 1 directs the specified census and issuance of findings upon completion; it does not establish performance.
Full paragraph authorizes temporary personnel, compensation, and expenditures necessary to carry out the August 30, 1937 act.
Final paragraph specifies allocations not exceeding $5,000,000 from the 1937 relief appropriation.

Held EO 7999 confirms the named office's records and property transfer effective November 1, 1938, its reference to EO 7711, signature date, and publication page. It does not terminate all EO 7711 authority.

The text says four named employees 'may be appointed,' subject to qualifications; it does not move staff automatically. 'Have served' does not establish that their service or the Administrator's duties ended.

Opened official statute text, page 883, confirms the April 1, 1938 census deadline. This proves neither completion nor expiration. Screenshot retrieval failed, so the worker's claimed image inspection is not independently confirmed.
Cited catalogue URL was inaccessible. The supplied title quotation establishes neither four volumes, publication details, Biggers's role, nor issuance by November 1, 1938.

Full held EO 7999 contains the records/property transfer and conditional appointment permission, without an express revocation, supersession, or textual amendment of EO 7711. This does not disprove the finding aid's broader amendment classification.

Opened act contains no express agency termination date and provides for temporary personnel. Its census deadline is not an agency sunset; 'only' is sustainable as a distinction from termination, not a description of all statutory powers.

stop_code_verdict: confirmed: WEB fits the first gap. The evidence slice supplies no final report or proof of issuance; the held transfer order does not resolve that fact, and the cited external catalogue remains inaccessible.
